blocks.text: 当模型反复调用一个失败的工具、而且参数往往一模一样时，AI 智能体就会陷入死循环，因为智能体循环里没有任何机制叫它停下来。每次重试都会把整段对话重新发一遍，于是每一轮都比上一轮更贵，一个跑了一整夜的空转循环可能烧掉数千美元。

inlines.text: 当模型反复调用一个失败的工具、而且参数往往一模一样时，AI 智能体就会陷入死循环，因为智能体循环里没有任何机制叫它停下来。每次重试都会把整段对话重新发一遍，于是每一轮都比上一轮更贵，一个跑了一整夜的空转循环可能烧掉数千美元。

blocks.text: 本指南用四道防线把循环拦住，我们在六个当前模型上做了测试。其中三道通过 OpenRouter Agent SDK（@openrouter/agent 0.11.0）运行在你的智能体内部：死循环检测、判定哪些调用算重复的规则，以及对步数和成本的上限。第四道是你 API 密钥上的额度上限。这道防线由我们这边执行，所以即使你的智能体代码有 bug 也依然有效。

blocks.text: TL;DR

inlines.text: TL;DR
开启死循环检测后，我们测试的六个模型全部在第三次相同的工具调用时被拦下。不开启时，18 次运行中有 4 次一直重试到 40 步上限。开启后，18 次运行中有 16 次在两次真实的工具调用后就结束了。
在 callModel 里设置 doomLoop: true，会拦下第三次相同的调用，并在第六次时结束运行。
有些模型会稍微改动参数来绕过检测。用一个对参数做归一化的 loopKey 就能拦住它们。
stopWhen: [stepCountIs(n), maxCost(x)] 会给每次运行设上限，不管循环是什么原因引起的。
密钥上的额度上限则封顶你的总花费。放不下的请求会失败，返回 402 和 limit_source: “openrouter_key_limit”。

blocks.text: 为什么 AI 智能体会陷入死循环？

inlines.text: 为什么 AI 智能体会陷入死循环？

blocks.text: 当模型不请求工具、直接给出回答时，智能体循环就结束了。而一个持续失败的工具，让模型没有理由这么做。错误被送回对话里，指令仍然要求完成任务，于是再试一次看起来就是正确的下一步。除非你加上代码去计数，否则循环里没有任何东西会统计尝试次数。

inlines.text: 当模型不请求工具、直接给出回答时，智能体循环就结束了。而一个持续失败的工具，让模型没有理由这么做。错误被送回对话里，指令仍然要求完成任务，于是再试一次看起来就是正确的下一步。除非你加上代码去计数，否则循环里没有任何东西会统计尝试次数。

blocks.text: 循环还会越跑越贵，因为每一轮都会把整段对话重新发一遍，包括之前每一次失败。在一次运行中我们逐轮做了记录，输入从 131 个 token 涨到 3,262 个，每轮成本几乎翻了两番。如果换成更贵的模型、同时跑很多会话，这种增长正是一夜之间累积到数千美元的原因。

死循环检测会按工具名和参数为每次工具调用生成指纹。它先对参数做规范化处理，所以即使 JSON 键的顺序被打乱，也无法掩盖重复。只有模型已经看到上一次结果、却再次发起请求时，才算一次重复，因此同一轮里五次完全相同的调用只计为一次。随着连续重复次数增加，它会沿默认阶梯逐级升级：2 次时观察，3 次时拦截，6 次时终止。

blocks.text: 调用被拦截时，SDK 会跳过 execute，并返回一个工具错误，告诉模型它正在重复自己。与超时不同，这个错误明确表示再试一次也没用。在大多数运行中，模型读到它后就直接写出最终答案，以 SessionEnd: complete 结束。在上面那次运行中，模型仍继续请求，于是 stop 以 reason: doom_loop 终止了运行。getDoomLoopVerdict() 只在检测导致运行结束时才返回消息，因此它是应当触发告警的信号。

DoomLoopDetected: observe (streak 2)

  fetch_invoice("inv-2291")
  fetch_invoice("INV-2291")
DoomLoopDetected: observe (streak 2)

blocks.text: stopWhen 在每一轮之后检查，只要任一条件为真，运行就停止。maxCost 会累加我们在每个响应中返回的 usage.cost，因此统计的是你实际被计费的部分。失败计数器忽略参数，所以即使没有 loopKey，也能抓住第 2 步里那种改动参数的情况。在一次以同样方式改动参数的 Mistral Large 4 运行中，它在六次调用后以 $0.0062 结束了会话，SessionEnd: max_turns。

blocks.text: 每个 stopWhen 条件都会以 reason: max_turns 结束会话，所以如果需要区分是哪个上限触发的，就得自己记录原因。如果上限触发时模型还有待执行的工具调用，SDK 会先把它们跑完，再在禁用工具调用的情况下做最后一轮，让这次运行以一段文字回答收尾。这就是为什么这次运行在上限为五的情况下发出了六次调用，也是为什么第一个演示在上限为四十的情况下跑了四十一次。把 allowFinalResponse 设为 false 可以跳过这一轮。

blocks.text: 两个上限都按你平时的运行情况来设。我们的运行用了四到六轮，在 Mistral Large 4 上花费 $0.0018 到 $0.0053，所以 15 步和 $0.01 留有余地，又不至于放任一次 40 轮的运行。两者之中，成本上限更重要，因为后面的轮次比前面的更贵。

blocks.text: 最大迭代次数限制能阻止成本失控吗？

inlines.text: 最大迭代次数限制能阻止成本失控吗？

blocks.text: 最大迭代次数限制能阻止单次运行无限进行下去，但它并不能限制你的花费，因为越往后的轮次成本越高，而且多次运行即使都在限制之内，加起来仍然很可观。LangChain 的 AgentExecutor 中的 max_iterations 和 CrewAI 中的 max_iter 这类设置，与 OpenRouter Agent SDK 中的 stepCountIs 作用相同。要把它们与单次运行的成本上限以及 API 密钥的额度限制配合使用。

blocks.text: An AI agent gets stuck in an infinite loop when a model keeps calling a tool that fails, usually with the same arguments, because nothing in the agent loop tells it to stop. Each retry resends the whole conversation, so every turn costs more than the last, and a loop left running overnight can cost thousands of dollars.

inlines.text: An AI agent gets stuck in an infinite loop when a model keeps calling a tool that fails, usually with the same arguments, because nothing in the agent loop tells it to stop. Each retry resends the whole conversation, so every turn costs more than the last, and a loop left running overnight can cost thousands of dollars.

blocks.text: This guide stops the loop with four guards, which we tested on six current models. Three run inside your agent through the OpenRouter Agent SDK (@openrouter/agent 0.11.0): doom-loop detection, a rule for which calls count as repeats, and caps on steps and cost. The fourth is a credit limit on your API key. We enforce it on our side, so it holds even when your agent code has a bug.

inlines.text: This guide stops the loop with four guards, which we tested on six current models. Three run inside your agent through the
OpenRouter Agent SDK

(@openrouter/agent 0.11.0): doom-loop detection, a rule for which calls count as repeats, and caps on steps and cost. The fourth is a credit limit on your API key. We enforce it on our side, so it holds even when your agent code has a bug.

blocks.text: TL;DR

inlines.text: TL;DR

With doom-loop detection on, all six models we tested were blocked on their third identical tool call. Without it, 4 of 18 runs retried until a 40-step cap. With it, 16 of 18 runs ended after two real tool calls.
doomLoop: true in callModel blocks the third identical call and ends the run at the sixth.
Some models get past detection by changing the argument slightly. A loopKey that normalizes the argument stops them.
stopWhen: [stepCountIs(n), maxCost(x)] caps every run, whatever causes the loop.
A credit limit on the key caps your total spend. A request that doesn’t fit fails with a 402 and limit_source: “openrouter_key_limit”.

blocks.text: Why do AI agents get stuck in infinite loops?

inlines.text: Why do AI agents get stuck in infinite loops?

blocks.text: An agent loop ends when the model answers without asking for a tool. A tool that keeps failing gives the model no reason to do that. The error goes back into the conversation, the instructions still say to finish the task, and another attempt looks like the right next step. Nothing in the loop counts attempts unless you add code that does.

inlines.text: An agent loop ends when the model answers without asking for a tool. A tool that keeps failing gives the model no reason to do that. The error goes back into the conversation, the instructions still say to finish the task, and another attempt looks like the right next step. Nothing in the loop counts attempts unless you add code that does.

blocks.text: The loop also gets more expensive as it goes, because every turn resends the whole conversation, including every earlier failure. In one run we logged turn by turn, input grew from 131 tokens to 3,262, and the cost per turn nearly quadrupled. With a pricier model and many sessions running at once, that growth is how one night adds up to thousands of dollars.

I was unable to retrieve the total for invoice INV-2291. The billing service
consistently timed out after 30 seconds on all 41 attempts to fetch this invoice, r

All 41 calls were identical, and the run ended only because of stepCountIs(40). The extra call is one the model had already asked for when the cap fired, which the SDK still runs (Step 3 covers this). Without a stopWhen, the Agent SDK keeps looping until the model stops asking for tools, so this run wouldn’t have stopped on its own. The final answer says the service was timing out, so the model knew that on every turn and retried anyway.

blocks.text: doomLoop: true,

fetch_invoice("INV-2291")
DoomLoopDetected: observe (streak 2)
  fetch_invoice("INV-2291")
DoomLoopDetected: block (streak 3)
DoomLoopDetected: block (streak 4)
DoomLoopDetected: block (streak 5)
DoomLoopDetected: stop (streak 6)
SessionEnd: doom_loop
attempts: 2, cost: $0.0034
stopped: Doom loop suspected: tool "fetch_invoice" was invoked in 6 consecutive rounds
with identical arguments (fingerprint 64be4614c5ea3e26…). Repeating the call will not
change the result. Take a different approach, or explain why repetition is required.

Doom-loop detection fingerprints each tool call by its name and arguments. It canonicalizes the arguments first, so reordered JSON keys don’t hide a repeat. A repeat only counts when the model has seen the previous result and asks again, so five identical calls in one turn count as one. As the streak grows, it climbs the default ladder: observe at 2, block at 3 and stop at 6.

blocks.text: When a call is blocked, the SDK skips execute and returns a tool error telling the model it’s repeating itself. Unlike the timeout, this error says another try won’t help. In most runs, the model read it and wrote a final answer straight away, ending with SessionEnd: complete. In the run above it kept asking, so stop ended the run with reason: doom_loop. getDoomLoopVerdict() returns a message only when detection ended the run, which makes it the signal to alert on.

blocks.text: To stop sooner, lower the thresholds. With doomLoop: { ladder: { observe: 2, block: 3, stop: 4 } }, a GPT-6 Luna run ended at streak 4 for $0.0002. The ladder also has two rungs that are off by default. steer sends the model a note that it’s repeating itself, and escalate runs the next turn on a stronger model you pick.

blocks.text: Normalize case, spacing, prefixes and anything else that doesn’t change which record the tool fetches. To ignore a field entirely, like a timeout the model raises on each retry, list only the fields that matter: loopKey: [‘invoice_id’]. A tool whose job is to repeat, like one that polls a job’s status, takes loopKey: false.

blocks.text: Every stopWhen condition ends the session with reason: max_turns, so log your own reason if you need to tell the caps apart. When a cap fires while the model still has tool calls pending, the SDK runs them and makes one last turn with tool calling disabled, so the run ends with a written answer. That’s why this run made six calls against a cap of five, and why the first demo made 41 against a cap of 40. Set allowFinalResponse: false to skip that turn.

blocks.text: Every guard so far runs inside your agent’s process. If that code has a bug, ships without the caps, or runs a hundred sessions that each stay under maxCost, nothing limits the total. A credit limit on the key does, because we check it on our side before the request reaches a provider.

blocks.text: Set limit (in dollars) and limit_reset (daily, weekly, monthly or null) in the dashboard or with the create key API. If the key uses BYOK, also set include_byok_in_limit to true, because it defaults to false and BYOK spend doesn’t count toward the limit otherwise. Daily limits reset at midnight UTC, and weekly limits reset on Monday. Give each agent or customer its own key, so one loop can only spend that key’s share. If several agents have to share a key, follow Capping Shared Agent Keys.

blocks.text: Branch on error.metadata.limit_source, not on the message text or the status code. An exhausted key also reports openrouter_key_limit, and the limits docs list that source under both 402 credit errors and 403 budget errors. If the message says the key can afford fewer tokens, as in the example above, retry with a lower max_tokens. If the key is exhausted, retrying can’t succeed until the limit resets, so treat it as a stop. The Agent SDK throws the 402 as PaymentRequiredResponseError. The one 402 worth retrying is openrouter_in_flight_budget, after its Retry-After header. Rate limits return 429 instead, which our LLM API rate limits guide covers.

blocks.text: Workspace budgets pool the cap across every key in a workspace, per day, week, month or lifetime. Blocked requests get a 403 with a message like Workspace monthly budget of $500.00 exceeded. Contact your org admin. (We didn’t trigger this one, so the message comes from the docs.) Requests already in flight still finish, so spend can go slightly over, but a loop that runs all night stops close to the daily cap. The spend controls guide shows how workspace budgets and per-member guardrails fit together.

blocks.text: Why does my agent keep calling the same tool after an error?

inlines.text: Why does my agent keep calling the same tool after an error?

blocks.text: The tool result says the call failed and the prompt says to finish the task, so another try looks like the right move to the model. Return errors that tell the model what to do next, like “The billing service is down. Tell the user and stop.” Don’t tell the model to retry until it succeeds.

blocks.text: Does a max iterations limit stop runaway costs?

inlines.text: Does a max iterations limit stop runaway costs?

blocks.text: A max iterations limit stops a single run from going on forever, but it doesn’t cap what you spend, because later turns cost more and many runs under the limit still add up. Settings like max_iterations in LangChain’s AgentExecutor and max_iter in CrewAI do the same job as stepCountIs in the OpenRouter Agent SDK. Pair one with a cost cap per run and a credit limit on the API key.
